ASML.priced_in_assessment: Heavily priced. Every pillar of the thesis — two guidance raises to EUR43-45B, 2027 EUV output sold out, +30% 2027 capacity with another +30% for 2028 'under study' — was stated publicly on the Q2 call. There is zero informational edge; the edge, if any, is durational: consensus 2028-29 models do not yet embed the second +30% capacity step, so conditional on the house singularity-2027 view (compute-gated adoption), out-year estimates are too low. But you pay ~49x screen / low-40s true forward vs a ~25x 10-yr median — roughly 1.7-2.0x the historical multiple — for that optionality.
ASML.strongest_counterargument: You are paying a peak multiple on potentially peak-cycle orders. The last time ASML was 'sold out with orders raised twice' was 2021; the stock then fell ~50% in 2022 despite the EUV monopoly being fully intact — IP-moat rent persistence protects the BUSINESS, not the entry multiple. A mean-reversion from ~42-49x to 30x is a -30-40% drawdown even with EPS growing. Meanwhile the marginal news flow is negative: the MATCH Act would extend US controls to all immersion DUV, directly threatening the ~20% of sales still going to China; China DUV demand is widely viewed as pull-forward that reverses regardless.
failure_modes: MATCH Act (or equivalent) passes and immersion DUV to China goes to ~zero: ~20% of revenue at risk, guidance cut, multiple derates simultaneously (double whammy)
2027 'sold out' proves to be hyperscaler/foundry over-ordering; 2028 +30% study is shelved and order pushouts appear (2021-22 replay)
AI capex digestion year in 2027: even a pause, not a bust, compresses a 40x+ multiple violently
Intel/Samsung customer wobble concentrates High-NA demand on TSMC alone, slowing the next-gen ASP mix story
Algorithmic efficiency gains reduce marginal litho intensity per unit of AI capability, softening the compute-gated-adoption link
ASML.structural_risks: Minimal structural risk for a long: ~1% short interest, no squeeze dynamics, un-acquirable, top index weight with passive bid. Real structural exposures are EUR/USD translation on the ADR and single-bill headline risk (MATCH Act) that can gap the stock 8-10% overnight (options imply ~8% earnings swings).
ASML.residual_trade: Do not chase at ~$1,770 after the beat. Scale in on China/export-control headline dips (the April MATCH-Act scare produced one; expect more) targeting an effective entry nearer 35x forward. Monitor: quarterly bookings/backlog vs the '2027 sold out' claim, formal 2028 +30% capacity commitment (upgrade trigger), MATCH Act legislative progress (invalidation trigger if it passes covering immersion DUV), and China % of sales trajectory. Hard invalidation: any customer pushout of 2027 EUV slots — the thesis dies before the tape shows it.
ASML.better_expression: TSMC (TSM) at roughly half the forward multiple captures the identical compute-buildout rent one node downstream, with its own effective monopoly (leading-edge foundry) and less single-bill China headline risk to reported revenue; a barbell of TSM plus a smaller ASML position beats a full-size ASML long at 40x+ on risk/reward.

CEG.priced_in_assessment: Less priced than the thesis assumed: the stock is at ~24x forward vs the 26-32x band the thesis was prepared to pay, after the early-July washout to $240. The July 14 PJM clear (all 18,875 MW at $325) and the Walmart/Dresden PPA are now public and drove the rebound to ~$275, so the easy 12% is gone — but 20-yr contracted hyperscaler PPAs (MSFT/Crane 2027, Meta/Clinton) plus the nuclear PTC floor are a genuinely asymmetric earnings floor that a 24x multiple does not fully credit if the 'contracted vs competed' distinction is right.
CEG.strongest_counterargument: The auction clearing at exactly $325/MW-day across all zones means it cleared AT the politically negotiated cap — the uncapped scarcity rent would have been higher, which is proof that regulators are already clipping the merchant portion of CEG's rent. The 'royalty-acre' framing overstates contract coverage: Crane (~835MW) and Clinton (~1.1GW) are a small slice of ~15.7GW of PJM nuclear plus the Calpine gas fleet; the majority of EBITDA remains merchant power and gas-spark-spread exposure, and the Calpine deal added roughly $12B of assumed net debt while DILUTING the nuclear-scarcity purity the thesis is buying. Consumer-bill backlash is the live political vector: caps can tighten, FERC can restrict co-location deals, and states can claw back 'windfall' rents.
failure_modes: Regulatory ratchet: PJM cap lowered or extended, FERC blocks/burdens co-located datacenter PPAs, state windfall levies — the exact scenario the $325-at-cap print foreshadows
AI datacenter capex digestion in 2027 removes the forward PPA pipeline narrative; multiple reverts toward merchant-peer 15-18x (-25-35%)
Crane restart slips past 2027 or has cost overruns (first-of-kind restart execution risk)
Gas prices fall and stay low: Calpine spark spreads and merchant nuclear margins compress together
SMR/new-build announcements erode the 'existing nuclear is irreplaceable scarcity' premium by 2029-30
CEG.structural_risks: Long-side structural picture is acceptable: SI ~3.4% and falling, no squeeze exposure. Balance sheet is the watch item — Calpine leverage plus 20% growth commitments narrows room for buybacks if power prices soften. Index/flow tailwind from AI-power thematic funds is real but reflexive in both directions.
CEG.residual_trade: Keep the long, entered on weakness not strength: the early-July $240s was the entry; at $275 add only on pullbacks toward $255-260. Monitor: Crane restart milestones (NRC approvals, fuel load — the 2027 in-service date is the thesis's proof point), each new hyperscaler PPA (converts merchant rent to contracted rent = multiple support), PJM/FERC/Pennsylvania political developments on caps and co-location, and gas curve. Invalidation: Crane slip beyond 2027, any cap tightening below $325, or a quarter where no new datacenter PPA is signed while peers announce them.

MAN.priced_in_assessment: The market is not mispricing robotics timing — it is repricing a cyclical trough exit that the shorts (19.9% of float) had bet against and just lost: Q2 EPS $0.99 vs $0.95-0.96 consensus, revenue +7.5-8% yoy as the first broad recovery print, Q3 guided to $0.96-1.06 (midpoint above Q2). At 14x forward on depressed cyclical EPS, nothing about a 2028+ robotics substitution wave is in, or needs to be in, the 2026 price — the market is not 'dating substitution beyond its horizon,' it is correctly refusing to pay for a thesis with no observable deployment data yet.
MAN.strongest_counterargument: This is a freshly detonated crowded short with a fundamental tailwind: 19.9% of float short, +34.8% in one day explicitly attributed to a squeeze, UBS already upgrading, and mean analyst targets below spot guaranteeing a conveyor belt of capitulation upgrades as further squeeze fuel. Even if the 2028 robotics thesis is 100% right, you can lose 50-80% of the position before a single robot displaces a single Manpower placement — and the thesis's own timeline (robotics ramp 2028+) means 18+ months of negative carry, borrow fees on crowded stock, and an accelerating EPS revision cycle against you. Wrong timing on a right thesis is just a wrong trade.
failure_modes: Continued squeeze: 6.75M shares short vs a small $2.4B cap; each beat/upgrade forces covering into thin float
Cyclical earnings recovery: staffing EPS can double off trough before any secular decline bites; 14x on $3.66 becomes 10x on $5+ and the stock re-rates up
Take-private/M&A: sub-$2.5B staffing platform with global brand is a plausible PE or Adecco/Randstad target; short gets bought in at a 30-40% premium
Timeline mismatch with the fund's own house view: software singularity 2027 hits COGNITIVE work first, robotics 2028+ — MAN's industrial staffing is the LAST staffing segment the thesis touches
Adaptation: Manpower monetizes the transition itself (reskilling, workforce-transition services, robot-adjacent light-industrial redeployment)
MAN.structural_risks: Maximal: crowded borrow at ~20% of float with rising fees and recall risk, momentum tape post-squeeze, small-cap take-private optionality, sell-side upgrade cycle just beginning, and management buyback capacity into any weakness. Every structural factor lines up against the short right now.
MAN.residual_trade: Killed. What revives it: (1) squeeze exhaustion — SI back under ~8% of float and sell-side targets caught up above spot; (2) first hard evidence of robot deployments hitting light-industrial staffing hours/bill rates in MAN's own KPIs (watch Manpower-brand US/Europe organic growth turning negative while GDP holds); (3) express via long-dated (2028) puts instead of stock borrow so the timeline mismatch and squeeze risk are capped at premium. Until then, no position.
MAN.better_expression: If the house view is software-first (2027) / robotics-later (2028+), the aligned staffing short is white-collar, not industrial: Robert Half (RHI) — accounting, finance, admin and IT contract staffing is precisely the cognitive work the 2027 leg automates, its secular decline is already observable in falling placements, and it carries far less squeeze setup than MAN. Short RHI (or Kforce) now; revisit industrial names like MAN in 2027-28 when robot deployment data exists.

6324.T.priced_in_assessment: Nothing of the bear case is in the price — and that is exactly the problem. The profit collapse (-54%), the share loss (global harmonic share from ~70% to ~18-20%), and Leaderdrive selling at 40-60% of HDS prices into Tesla/Figure are all extensively public (multiple mid-2026 articles literally titled 'valuation ignores both'), yet the stock is +143% anyway. Price embeds p90 humanoid volumes WITH retained Western share and margins (~145x even on the aggressive +180% NI rebound guide, ~$50M of humanoid orders supporting a $4.4B cap). This means valuation is not the current pricing mechanism — narrative is — so the short's edge cannot cash until the narrative breaks, and the analyst range findable (JPY 7,800-11,000 vs 6,570 spot) suggests the sell side is still above the price.
6324.T.strongest_counterargument: The fund's own macro thesis kills the timing: if robotics ramps 2028+, then 2026-27 is the maximum-hype phase for THE Japan humanoid pure-play, and the fundamental unmasking (Chinese reducers winning the volume, HDS margins compressing) only becomes visible in reported numbers in 2027-28. Concretely: Tesla Optimus Gen3 mass production starts Q3 2026 — i.e., within weeks of entry — and the company is guiding humanoid orders to double-or-triple in FY3/27 (JPY 2.5B -> ~7.5B), so the next 2-4 quarterly prints are order-growth headlines, each a squeeze catalyst in a stock that just did +143%/12mo with unknowable Japanese borrow. Corning didn't break in 1999; it broke in late 2000. This is 1999. And HDS has sustained >100-150x P/E for years (2017-21) — the multiple alone has never been the catalyst; it took macro downturns.
failure_modes: Squeeze on humanoid order headlines: Optimus Gen3 mass production starting Q3 2026, FY3/27 order-tripling prints, Figure/Boston Dynamics design wins

Western supply-chain bifurcation: US/EU humanoid makers derisk from Chinese components (export controls, defense-adjacent buyers), leaving HDS the non-China monopolist with restored pricing power — thesis inverts
Cyclical earnings recovery: FY3/26 collapse was partly industrial-robot/semi-cycle; the guided +180% NI rebound optically compresses the P/E fast and gives bulls cover
Borrow tightness/recall in a Japanese mid-cap after a +143% run; JPX lending restrictions can hit exactly when the stock rips; >0.5% short positions are publicly disclosed, painting a target
Nikkei 225 membership: passive flows and index-linked buying amplify upside moves
JPY translation risk on a USD book layered on top of single-name risk
6324.T.structural_risks: Borrow unverifiable and likely tight/expensive post-run (short interest data not findable — itself a red flag for sizing); Japanese retail margin-buying dynamics produce 30-50% monthly rips in narrative names; Nikkei 225 passive flows; public short-position disclosure above 0.5%; take-private/M&A risk low at this valuation (only mitigant), Nabtesco cross-holding is passive.
6324.T.residual_trade: KILLED as an outright short today. Revive via any of: (1) long-dated put spreads sized to survive the stock doubling first — defined-risk is the only acceptable naked-direction expression in a narrative stock pre-catalyst-exhaustion; (2) outright short triggered by the first humanoid-order disappointment (any FY3/27 quarter where humanoid orders undershoot the double-to-triple guide, or company walks it back) or by an Optimus Gen3 teardown confirming Chinese reducer majority share at HDS's expense; (3) pair: short 6324 vs long a robot-theme long leg to strip hype beta (see better_expression). Invalidation of the revived short: HDS wins a sole-source Western humanoid platform at maintained gross margins, or US export-control action functionally bans Chinese reducers from US robot programs.
6324.T.better_expression: Pair trade: short 6324.T vs long Nabtesco (6268.T, ~20x P/E, RV-gear analog in the same robot-reducer theme) or a Japan robot basket — isolates the share-loss/valuation-gap alpha while neutralizing the humanoid-hype factor and yen beta that make the naked short lethal. If the real view is 'Chinese reducers win the volume,' the direct long is Leaderdrive itself (Leader Harmonious Drive, 688017.SS) rather than a Japan short, though its own multiple needs the same scrutiny.

PLTR.priced_in_assessment: Partially deflated, still priced for near-perfection. The -26% to -40% 2026 drawdown ('SaaSpocalypse') means the market has ALREADY priced the first wave of the agents-commoditize-software fear — the short thesis is now the consensus narrative, not a variant view. But what remains embedded is still extreme: ~42x the raised FY26 revenue guide ($7.65B), ~88x forward earnings, ~59x trailing sales — a price that requires durable 50%+ growth and 40%+ margins into 2029-30. NOT yet priced: any actual deceleration (fundamentals are accelerating — Q1 revenue +85% to $1.63B, US commercial +133%, Rule of 40 at 145) or gross-margin erosion from open-source agent stacks (zero evidence in numbers to date). The key priced-in insight favoring the short: the stock fell 30-40% WHILE printing its best quarters ever — good news no longer lifts the price, the classic Cisco-2000 distribution pattern where deflation from 97x forward earnings does not stop at 88x.
PLTR.strongest_counterargument: You are shorting a company whose growth is ACCELERATING (85% yoy, guide raised to +71% FY26, US commercial +133%) ten days before an Aug 3 earnings print, on a commoditization mechanism that has it backwards so far: AIP is positioned as the agent-deployment/ontology layer, so AI agents are currently DRIVING Palantir demand, not displacing it — the acceleration is the direct empirical refutation of the thesis to date. At consensus FY27 revenue of ~$11.2B the stock de-rates to ~29x sales through growth alone (~45%/yr multiple compression with zero price decline), the government segment (accreditations, multi-year contracts) is immune to open-source stacks on any 2026-27 timeline, and the register of history: pure valuation shorts against 70-85% compounders (PLTR itself 2023-25, TSLA 2020) are widow-makers until deceleration shows up in a print. It hasn't.
failure_modes: Aug 3 beat-and-raise gamma/retail squeeze — PLTR has a history of +15-25% earnings-day moves on a cult retail base and massive options market
Commoditization thesis inverts: AIP captures agent-deployment spend; every quarter of 70%+ growth extends the runway and burns carry
Government moat (FedRAMP/IL5-6, multi-year contracts, NATO/UK expansion) makes a large revenue block structurally un-commoditizable near-term; NHS scrutiny resolves favorably
Growth outruns compression: two more years of 60-80% growth normalizes the multiple without the price ever falling to the short's target
~$5-6B net cash, no debt, buyback authorization — balance-sheet optionality to defend the stock
S&P 500 mega-cap index flows and any AI-sentiment re-rally lift it 20-30% before thesis evidence arrives
PLTR.structural_risks: Short interest only ~3.6% of float — not crowded, borrow trivial and cheap, no recall risk (genuine positives). Offsetting: extreme retail/options-driven squeeze mechanics independent of SI; passive index support as a top-25 S&P weight; net-cash balance sheet with buyback capacity; no M&A/take-private risk at $323B. The structural setup is unusually clean for a mega-cap short — the risk is event-path (earnings), not plumbing.
PLTR.residual_trade: SURVIVES, restructured — the pitched version (naked short, now, on the commoditization story) is rejected on timing. Rules: (1) NO short exposure into the Aug 3 print — flat until it clears. (2) Post-print entry: short a failed rally / lower-high after results, or buy 3-6 month put spreads (defined risk against squeeze) if results merely meet. (3) Add only on evidence: first quarter with US commercial growth <70%, FY guidance implying H2 deceleration below ~50%, NRR compression, or a named open-source agent-stack displacement in a government or large commercial account. (4) Monitor: NHS/UK contract outcomes, the 'World Monitor' open-source rival traction, DoD budget language, insider selling cadence. (5) Hard invalidation: reclaim and hold above ~$160 (roughly half the drawdown retraced) alongside reaccelerating guidance — that means the SaaSpocalypse regime ended and the multiple is expanding again; cover, do not average.
PLTR.better_expression: The purer casualty of 'AI agents write arbitrary software' is billed-hours integration, not the agent substrate: short a basket of IT-services/bespoke-integration names (ACN, EPAM, GLOB, mid-tier SIs) whose revenue is literally the thing being commoditized and who lack PLTR's product moat, government accreditations, and 85% growth shield — several already show revenue deceleration, so the thesis has fundamental confirmation there that PLTR lacks. Alternatively express PLTR downside exclusively via put spreads to cap the earnings-squeeze tail.
